purpose: Stable project context for generating one accurate Git commit subject from staged FlashOS changes.

generation_contract.evidence: Only staged_file_status and staged_diff describe the current commit.
generation_contract.result: One locally validated English subject in the repository house style.
generation_contract.house_style: Conventional type with an optional lowercase scope, one imperative subject line, at most 72 characters, and no trailing period.
generation_contract.prohibited_inference: Do not use repository context, filenames alone, unstaged assumptions, milestone knowledge, or model repair feedback as evidence of a change.

context_policy.scope: Use these facts only to interpret the staged file status and staged diff. The context does not describe what changed in the current commit.
authority_order: The staged file status and staged diff are authoritative for what changed.
Executable code, configuration, recipes, and tests are authoritative for current behavior.
Public documentation and this context explain intent and terminology but do not prove implementation.
never_infer: Do not treat an unstaged, untracked, ignored, or merely referenced file as changed.
Do not claim that a referenced helper, package, component, driver, or feature was added unless the staged diff proves it.
Do not infer branch intent, release scope, milestone state, or current version unless the staged diff shows it.
Do not treat inherited or upstream code present in the repository as an active or qualified FlashOS capability.
Do not treat host-side behavior as target-image behavior.
Do not treat a successful build, test, or QEMU path as broader evidence than the changed contract explicitly supports.

project.name: FlashOS
project.identity: FlashOS is an independent operating-system project with its own identity, roadmap, configuration, verification contracts, and releases. It is not an official Redox OS distribution.
project.primary_evaluation_environment: QEMU q35 with x86_64 UEFI firmware
project.user_environment: A keyboard-driven, terminal-native, text-based environment without a graphical desktop environment.
strategic_direction: The current product path is x86_64 first.
AArch64 is a later platform initiative and is not current release support.
The long-term intended borrowed boundary is the kernel; other inherited Redox dependencies are transitional and are replaced only through deliberate changes.

terminology.flashos_command: The host-side shell helper command exposed by flashos.sh. It is development tooling and is not the target operating system or a target-side command unless a staged change explicitly installs it.
terminology.flashos_build: The root Rust package that supports host-side package and image construction. It is not the FlashOS kernel.
terminology.Flash: The FlashOS-owned interactive shell and scripting language. It is non-POSIX and is not a Bash or sh implementation.
terminology.Redox_names: Names such as x86_64-unknown-redox, relibc, redox_installer, RedoxFS, and redox-live.iso are compatibility or inherited build-interface names. Their presence does not change the FlashOS product identity.
terminology.TUI_only: TUI-only excludes desktop environments, window servers, GUI application sets, and graphical installers. It does not exclude framebuffer display, keyboard input, terminals, networking, storage, USB/PCI, or audio needed by the product.

flashos_owned: FlashOS-specific configuration and selected local patches
pinned_or_inherited: relibc and the Redox target ABI
root build orchestration inherited from and adapted from Redox
interpretation_rules: A local patch changes only the behavior shown by that patch; it does not make the complete upstream component FlashOS-native.
A recipe defines how a package is obtained or built; it does not by itself prove that the package is selected by an image profile.
A selected package may pull additional dependencies; do not describe the full resolved package graph unless the diff proves it.
A source change in Flash does not automatically reach an image; the image recipe uses a pinned repository revision.

host.description: Development machine and hosted CI environment that produce and inspect artifacts.

target.description: The generated FlashOS image and its runtime.
boot_flow: pinned Redox kernel with local FlashOS changes
Flash built-ins or external userspace processes

execution_environments.boundary_rule: Host utilities, host tests, container dependencies, and development integrations are not automatically installed in or supported by the target image.

repository_map.role: Host-side FlashOS developer command interface, shell completion, AI helpers, and stable AI project context.
semantic_hints: Dispatcher, usage, and completion edits usually expose or wire a command.
The Python helpers under tools/flashos implement host-side developer commands and shared AI functionality.
The JSON files under tools/flashos/contexts provide stable project context but do not prove the current staged change.
Referencing an external helper script does not prove that the helper was added or implemented in the same diff.
Changes here are normally host tooling, not target operating-system functionality.

repository_map.role: Host-side build orchestration, configuration resolution, toolchain support, package cooking, image assembly, and QEMU invocation.
semantic_hints: The root Rust crate is build-system support, not kernel code.
Use build: for build-system behavior unless another commit type more precisely describes the primary effect.

repository_map.role: Host bootstrap and containerized build environment.
semantic_hints: Container changes affect the build boundary, not the FlashOS runtime unless the diff also changes produced image contents.

repository_map.role: Shared TUI-oriented product foundation for FlashOS image profiles.
semantic_hints: Changes can affect package selection, filesystem layout, scheme permissions, networking, services, or shared installed files.

repository_map.role: x86_64 development image profile.
semantic_hints: Defines development-image settings, users, credentials, installed files, startup behavior, and login shells.

repository_map.role: x86_64 release image profile.
semantic_hints: The release profile is intended to align with the development profile except for the credential model and release-specific restrictions.

repository_map.role: Pinned package sources, package build rules, dependencies, patches, and installed package contents.
semantic_hints: A recipe change affects package construction or integration.
A package becomes part of FlashOS only when selected by the active profile directly or through a required dependency.
recipes/core/kernel/** and recipes/core/bootloader/** remain upstream-component boundaries even when locally patched.
recipes/terminal/flash/** integrates a pinned Flash revision into images.

repository_map.role: Independent in-tree Rust workspace for Flash.
semantic_hints: Syntax, runtime, platform contracts, POSIX/Redox integration, terminal behavior, process execution, and the fsh CLI live here.
Host behavior does not prove Redox-target or image behavior.
Flash is non-POSIX and launches external executables directly through its platform layer.

repository_map.role: Lexing, parsing, syntax trees, source representation, and diagnostics.
Runtime values, evaluation, built-ins, execution plans, sessions, pipelines, jobs, and status behavior.
Platform capability contracts used by the Flash runtime.
Process, filesystem, descriptor, signal, process-group, and terminal integration for supported platforms.
The fsh executable, interactive front end, script entry point, startup, history, and line-editing integration.
Static product-profile and repository invariant checks.
semantic_hints: Passing this check proves only the encoded static contract; it does not compile packages, build images, or boot FlashOS.

repository_map.role: Runtime qualification for exact built images in defined x86_64 QEMU paths.
semantic_hints: QEMU qualification does not establish physical hardware compatibility.

repository_map.role: Local executable product, image, runtime, and CI contracts.
Hosted source-quality, product-contract, clean image-build, artifact-promotion, and QEMU qualification workflows.
Dependency review and Cargo supply-chain policy checks.
Tag validation, release image qualification, packaging, checksums, SBOMs, provenance, and publication.
Central FlashOS release-version source.
semantic_hints: Version commits must keep all version-bearing surfaces aligned when the staged diff shows a release change.

repository_map.role: Canonical public FlashOS overview, architecture, development, verification, hardware, roadmap, and user guidance.
semantic_hints: Documentation-only changes use docs: unless the staged diff also changes implementation or a stronger primary effect.
docs/upstream/** is retained reference material and does not define supported FlashOS behavior.

repository_map.role: Public Flash product, language, scripting, architecture, and development documentation.
Public FlashOS change history.
Security reporting process, evaluation limits, and security-related public claims.
Generated local artifacts and logs.
semantic_hints: Generated build outputs are not source and should normally remain untracked.

verification_model.principle: Each verification layer supports only a bounded claim.

layers.name: physical_hardware
layers.evidence: device-specific test record for an exact image and revision
layers.does_not_prove: support for other devices or revisions

layers.name: release_evidence
layers.evidence: qualified artifacts, checksums, SBOMs, and provenance
layers.does_not_prove: formal security assurance or bit-for-bit reproducibility

style: Summarize the primary staged effect rather than listing every touched file.
Prefer a concrete user-visible or repository-level effect over implementation nouns.
Use the current conventional house style consistently; do not imitate historical unprefixed subjects.
Do not mention AI vendors, model names, APIs, assistance, generation, or co-authorship in a commit subject, including for changes to the Gemini-backed host tools.
Do not mention how the subject was generated or any private planning or workflow metadata.
Do not mention internal phase, milestone, decision, handover, or private workspace identifiers.

type_meanings.feat:: Adds or exposes a user-visible or developer-visible capability.
type_meanings.fix:: Corrects incorrect behavior or a defect.
type_meanings.refactor:: Changes internal structure without intentionally changing behavior.
type_meanings.test:: Changes tests or test infrastructure without a broader primary product effect.
type_meanings.build:: Changes build tooling, package construction, dependencies, toolchains, or image assembly.
type_meanings.ci:: Changes hosted or local CI workflow contracts and automation.
type_meanings.chore:: Maintenance that does not fit a more precise type.
type_meanings.release:: Changes release versioning, release metadata, or release packaging as the primary effect.

scope_policy.format: A scope is lowercase ASCII alphanumeric text with optional internal hyphens, enclosed in parentheses between the type and colon.
scope_policy.use: Use a scope when one clear repository area owns the primary effect; omit it for repository-wide or naturally unscoped changes.

known_scopes.flash: Flash component source, tests, metadata, or component documentation under components/flash/.
known_scopes.tools: Host developer commands under flashos.sh, flashos.zsh, or tools/flashos/.
known_scopes.ci: A focused correction or feature in CI scripts or workflow behavior when the scope adds clarity. Pure workflow maintenance may use ci: without a scope.

rules: Use type(flash): for a primary Flash component effect; do not use the historical Flash: prefix.
Use type(tools): for a primary host developer-tool effect.
Do not add a scope merely because a touched path contains that word.
Do not invent issue numbers, milestone names, branch names, or private planning identifiers as scopes.

mixed_diff_rules: Choose the prefix and wording from the primary coherent effect, not the largest file.
If a diff combines unrelated effects, still describe only the dominant staged purpose; do not invent a common purpose.
A completion or help update that accompanies a new command is normally secondary to exposing the command.
A recipe revision update that makes existing component work available in images is an integration or pinning change, not a new implementation of that component.
